records.summary: LinkedIn Marketing APIs use three-legged OAuth 2.0 member access tokens and a versioned REST base path. Development access is the starting tier; Standard access requires a Developer Support ticket and LinkedIn review, with some private APIs requiring additional approval. No LinkedIn Ads vendor MCP server is documented in the targeted official Marketing pages.
records.blocker: Only ad accounts explicitly configured in the developer application can be managed. Standard access and private APIs require approval, and two-legged client credentials are unavailable for marketing use cases.
records.next_action: Create a LinkedIn developer application, request the required Marketing API program access and scopes, configure approved ad accounts, and use three-legged OAuth. Start in Development, test against supported accounts, then submit a Standard-access ticket through the Developer Support Portal.

records.summary: Telegram's Bot API is a broad HTTP-based interface authenticated by a unique bot token, with GET and POST methods and extensive messaging features. Bots can message users at no cost, subject to broadcast limits. Targeted official review found no Telegram-operated MCP server documented in the Bot Platform sources; this is a scoped documentation finding, not proof of universal absence.
records.blocker: No Telegram-operated MCP server is documented in the reviewed official Bot Platform sources; direct Bot API integration remains available. Bot capabilities also depend on chat membership and administrator-granted rights.
records.next_action: Create a bot through BotFather, protect its token, and build with the Bot API using only the chats and admin rights required. Use the documented Bot API rather than waiting for a Telegram MCP endpoint, and recheck official sources before adopting any future MCP integration.

auth.reason: Telegram states that each bot receives a unique authentication token and that bots are connected to a backend through the Bot API after setup with BotFather. The Bot API is dated November 22, 2026; the FAQ is undated.
